name: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)
short_description: A single continuous membrane network beginning right at the nuclear envelope that splits into two connected regions: ribosome-studded ROUGH ER (stacked cisternae) folding and quality-checking newly built proteins, transitioning into ribosome-free SMOOTH ER (branching tubules) that makes lipids and hormones, detoxifies, and stores calcium.

textbook.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; strong start on the rough-to-smooth contrast — a densely ribosome-dotted blue-grey band transitions cleanly into a bare pale-green branching tubule network, with transport vesicles and a small subordinate Golgi hint. Two misses: (a) no nuclear-envelope patch anywhere, so the ER reads as free-floating rather than growing out of the nucleus; (b) the 'rough ER' region reads as one continuous dotted blob rather than several distinct flattened sheets with visible lumen gaps between them. Fix-prompt: add a short double-line nuclear-envelope edge at one side that the rough-ER sheets visibly grow out of, and make the rough-ER region read as several separate parallel flat sheets, each with its own pale lumen gap before the next)
textbook.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; both fixes applied cleanly — a clear double-line nuclear-envelope edge sits at the left margin with the rough-ER sheets visibly flowing out of it; five distinct flattened parallel cisternae are now legible, each densely ribosome-studded on its outer edges with a pale lumen gap before the next, all connected (not disconnected Golgi-like discs); the sheets transition smoothly into a bare branching smooth-ER tubule network with no ribosome dots anywhere on it; transport vesicles bud near a small, clearly subordinate Golgi hint off to one side. Muted educational palette, thin outlines, neutral background, no text, no border. Used as the primary labelled figure)

sem.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; excellent false-colour contrast between a stack of clearly separate ribosome-studded cisternae and a bare pale-green smooth membrane surface — the core rough-vs-smooth textural contrast is immediately legible and convincing as SEM. Misses: the smooth region reads as a blank folded wall rather than a branching tubule network, and there is no nuclear-envelope connection anywhere in frame. Fix-prompt: add a nuclear-envelope patch at one edge continuous with the sheet stack, and give the smooth region visible branching tubule structure rather than a plain wall)
sem.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; a small ribosome-studded nuclear-envelope patch now sits at the left edge, directly continuous with the sheet stack; the smooth region now reads as a genuine branching, fenestrated tubular network (visible openings/holes between branches) rather than a blank wall; ribosome studding is dense and unmistakable on the sheets and completely absent from the tubules; two transport vesicles are visible near the transition. Crisp false-colour surface photorealism, shallow depth of field, cool studio lighting, no text, no border. Not labelled, per project convention for the SEM surface/comparison plate)

Warm aged paper fills the frame edge to edge with a soft wash halo, fine ink linework, no mat/frame/sheet-on-a-surface. Used for the labelled figure (black-on-paper ink per style convention))

reference: pass, with an honest caveat stated plainly (Wikimedia Commons "Clara cell lung - TEM.jpg", Public domain, Louisa Howard, Rippel Electron Microscope Facility, Dartmouth College - the same trusted source already used for this set's nucleus, mitochondrion and Golgi-apparatus plates. A genuine thin-section transmission electron micrograph unmistakably showing an exceptionally clear, extensive whorled stack of rough-ER cisternae filling most of the frame, alongside several mitochondria and part of a nucleus at lower right - real electron microscopy demonstrating that ER cisternae are continuous with each other, not separate discs. Caveat, stated honestly: this plate shows ROUGH ER ONLY - no smooth-ER tubule region is distinguishable in frame, and individual ribosome particles are only faintly resolvable at this compression (the sheets read as finely corrugated rather than crisply dotted). No freely-licensed plate found during research clearly captured both regions in one frame; that combination is genuinely rare since smooth ER is sparse in most ordinary cells and the two regions are often far apart in the cytosol. The illustrated styles carry the rough-to-smooth contrast explicitly as first-class labelled content, since this real micrograph cannot. Cleaned with a plain DETERMINISTIC CROP, not edit_image.py: the raw 640x480 download's baked-in footer band (500 nm scale bar, '06LungTEM', '1/7/0 REMF' instrument text, measured at rows y=455-479) was cropped away, the remaining 640x455 content centre-cropped to a 455x455 square, then upscaled 2.37x to 1080x1080 with LANCZOS - stated explicitly per instructions. No pixels invented or re-illustrated, only crop + resize
